name: Calcium
blurb: Calcium is everywhere in physiology and almost invisible to NMR: the only spin-bearing stable isotope, 43Ca, is 0.135 percent abundant with gamma of 2.87 MHz/T, giving a receptivity about 20 times below natural-abundance 13C. In clinical MR, calcium is seen indirectly, as the signal void of cortical bone and as the diamagnetic susceptibility of calcification.
mrNotes: Calcification is diamagnetic relative to tissue while iron is paramagnetic, so QSM separates the two where T2*-weighted magnitude cannot.
43Ca resonates at 8.6 MHz at 3 T, below the tuning range of most clinical multinuclear receive chains, and no in-vivo 43Ca spectrum has been reported.
41Ca is a long-term bone-resorption tracer read out by accelerator mass spectrometry, not by any MR or gamma-camera method.

isotopes.notes: Only NMR-active stable Ca isotope. Used in solid-state NMR of cements, apatites and Ca-binding proteins, almost always with 43Ca enrichment. Q revised to -4.44 fm2 by hyperfine-structure work on Ca+ (older tables give -4.08 fm2).
Long-lived (electron capture) bone tracer detected by AMS at 1e-17 isotopic ratios. Not an NMR nucleus; Q not well established, so listed as null.

name: Scandium
blurb: 45Sc is one of the easiest quadrupolar nuclei in the periodic table: 100 percent abundant, I = 7/2, receptivity about 0.30 of 1H, so natural-abundance spectra take seconds. Scandium has no biological role and no in-vivo MR use; its relevance to imaging is radionuclide, as the 44Sc/47Sc PET-plus-therapy pair.
mrNotes: 45Sc receptivity is roughly 1780 times natural-abundance 13C, behind only 93Nb, 51V, 115In and 141Pr among metals, every one of them quadrupolar.
44Sc (t1/2 3.97 h, positron emitter) and 47Sc (t1/2 3.35 d, beta minus) form a matched theranostic pair with the same chelation chemistry.
Scandium appears in no MR hardware, implant alloy or contrast agent.

isotopes.notes: Quadrupolar coupling constants of 3.9 to 13.1 MHz are typical and track the symmetry of the Sc coordination sphere; MQMAS is routine. No in-vivo use.

name: Titanium
blurb: Titanium is the dominant implant and device metal in MRI and it is half of NbTi, the superconductor wound into essentially every clinical magnet. As an NMR nucleus it is poor: 47Ti and 49Ti are both low-gamma quadrupolar nuclei whose Larmor frequencies sit only about 270 ppm apart, so they overlap in one spectrum.
mrNotes: NbTi filament wire, superconducting below about 9.2 K, carries the main solenoid of nearly all 1.5 T and 3 T clinical systems.
Ti-6Al-4V is weakly paramagnetic, volume susceptibility about +180 ppm SI, so its artifact is far smaller than stainless steel or CoCrMo, but it is not artifact free.

47Ti (I = 5/2) and 49Ti (I = 7/2) have nearly equal gamma, so both appear in every titanium spectrum and must be fitted jointly; their second-order quadrupolar broadenings differ, which is how they are told apart.
45Ti (t1/2 3.08 h) is an emerging PET nuclide; it is not used for NMR.

isotopes.notes: Broader than 49Ti at the same site because of its larger Q and lower spin. Solid-state 47/49Ti NMR usually needs 18.8 T or higher plus QCPMG.
Narrower central transition than 47Ti (higher spin, smaller Q) despite lower abundance, so 49Ti often dominates the usable signal.

name: Vanadium
blurb: 51V is the best-behaved quadrupolar transition-metal nucleus: 99.75 percent abundant, I = 7/2, and with an unusually small quadrupole moment, giving 38 percent of the receptivity of 1H. It has no in-vivo MR role but is the standard probe for vanadium oxide catalysts, vanadium redox-flow electrolytes and vanadate biochemistry.
mrNotes: 51V receptivity is about 2250 times natural-abundance 13C; a natural-abundance solution spectrum takes seconds.
Vanadium is a minority component of Ti-6Al-4V implant alloy; the susceptibility artifact of such implants is set by the titanium matrix, not the vanadium.
50V is 0.25 percent abundant with I = 6 and is effectively stable (t1/2 about 2.7e17 y); it contributes a weak second resonance about 2.6 times lower in frequency than 51V.

isotopes.notes: Small Q means narrow lines even in low-symmetry sites, which is why 51V solid-state NMR works where 53Cr and 55Mn struggle. Q is quoted here as -5.2 fm2; other compilations give -4.8 and -4.3 fm2, a 20 percent spread that this chart does not adjudicate.
Integer spin (I = 6), observationally stable, decaying by electron capture and beta minus. Q of +21 fm2 makes it much broader than 51V; rarely used except as a moment/Q cross-check.

name: Chromium
blurb: Chromium reaches MRI mainly through CoCrMo, the bearing alloy in hip and knee arthroplasty and one of the worst metal-artifact sources in orthopaedic imaging, and through 51Cr-EDTA, still a reference measurement of GFR. Elemental chromium is the textbook itinerant antiferromagnet, with a Neel temperature of 311 K.
mrNotes: CoCrMo has volume susceptibility of order +1000 ppm SI, several times titanium, so arthroplasty imaging needs view-angle tilting or SEMAC plus high readout bandwidth.
51Cr (t1/2 27.7 d, 320 keV gamma) labels red cells for blood-volume and red-cell-survival studies, and as 51Cr-EDTA gives a plasma-clearance GFR.
53Cr is the only NMR-active chromium isotope and is a genuinely hard nucleus: gamma 2.41 MHz/T, 9.5 percent abundant, receptivity about half that of natural-abundance 13C.

isotopes.notes: Usable only for high-symmetry diamagnetic Cr(0) and Cr(VI) species such as Cr(CO)6 and chromates; anything less symmetric is broadened beyond detection by the -15 fm2 quadrupole moment.
Electron-capture nuclide used for 51Cr-EDTA GFR and red-cell labelling. Magnetic moment -0.934(5) nuclear magnetons; Q not confidently tabulated, so null.

name: Manganese
blurb: Manganese is the paramagnetic ion behind manganese-enhanced MRI and behind the leading gadolinium-free T1 agents: Mn(II) is high-spin d5 with five unpaired electrons and a long electronic relaxation time, so it is an efficient T1 relaxer. 55Mn itself is a 100 percent abundant I = 5/2 nucleus with good in-vitro receptivity that is never detected in vivo.
mrNotes: Mn2+ enters cells through voltage-gated Ca2+ channels, which is what makes MEMRI a neuronal activity and tract-tracing method rather than just another T1 agent.
Mangafodipir (Mn-DPDP) was a clinical liver agent; Mn(II) and Mn(III) chelates are now in trials as gadolinium-free alternatives with r1 of roughly 2 to 6 s^-1 mM^-1 at 1.5 T.
Free Mn2+ is cardiotoxic and accumulates in basal ganglia (the T1-hyperintense globus pallidus of manganism), which is the dose limit on clinical MEMRI.
The in-vivo manganese signal is the proton T1 shortening it causes, not a 55Mn resonance; 55Mn NMR is an in-vitro and solid-state technique only.

isotopes.notes: Receptivity about 1050 times natural-abundance 13C, but the 33 fm2 quadrupole moment restricts solution work to near-tetrahedral or octahedral diamagnetic Mn, mainly permanganate and Mn carbonyls.

name: Iron
blurb: Iron dominates endogenous MR contrast: deoxyhaemoglobin iron is the source of BOLD, ferritin and haemosiderin drive T2* and QSM contrast in deep grey matter, haemorrhage and liver, and iron oxide nanoparticles are the main non-gadolinium contrast class. The NMR nucleus 57Fe is irrelevant by comparison, with gamma of 1.38 MHz/T at 2.1 percent abundance.
mrNotes: Deoxyhaemoglobin is paramagnetic and oxyhaemoglobin is diamagnetic; fully deoxygenated blood is shifted about 0.27 ppm per unit haematocrit from fully oxygenated, and that difference is the whole of BOLD.
Ferumoxytol is used off-label as a blood-pool and macrophage agent in patients who cannot receive gadolinium; its r2* is about 57 s^-1 mM^-1 at 3 T and about 60 s^-1 mM^-1 at 1.5 T.

Ferromagnetic steel is the principal projectile hazard at the 5 gauss line and the reason for ferromagnetic detection at the Zone IV door; soft iron is also the yoke and pole material of open and permanent-magnet systems.
57Fe receptivity is about 7e-7 of 1H, roughly 0.004 of natural-abundance 13C, so even in-vitro 57Fe NMR needs enrichment, and 57Fe is used far more as the Mossbauer isotope.

isotopes.notes: Spin 1/2, so no quadrupolar broadening, but among the smallest gyromagnetic ratios in routine use, in the same class as 103Rh and 187Os; T1 is long and enrichment is essentially mandatory. Chemical shift range exceeds 10000 ppm.

name: Cobalt
blurb: Cobalt is an implant metal (CoCrMo bearings and stents) and a permanent-magnet ingredient (SmCo, AlNiCo), and 60Co is the Gamma Knife and teletherapy source. 59Co has the largest chemical shift range of any nucleus, around 18000 ppm, and a shift that moves about 1.5 ppm per kelvin, which makes it a practical NMR thermometer.
mrNotes: CoCrMo femoral heads and stems are strongly paramagnetic and give the worst orthopaedic metal artifact after stainless steel; expect centimetre-scale signal voids and geometric distortion at 3 T.
59Co in K3[Co(CN)6] shifts about 1.5 ppm per K, so a 59Co sample is a convenient absolute-temperature reference in variable-temperature NMR.

60Co (t1/2 5.27 y, 1.17 and 1.33 MeV gammas) is the Gamma Knife and cobalt-60 teletherapy source; 57Co (t1/2 271.7 d) is the standard gamma-camera flood-field source and the Mossbauer source for 57Fe.
SmCo permanent magnets hold their magnetisation to high temperature and are used in small preclinical and single-sided MR magnets and in MR-compatible motors.

isotopes.notes: Receptivity over 1600 times natural-abundance 13C, so signal is never the problem; the 42 fm2 quadrupole moment is, and only near-octahedral diamagnetic Co(III) gives narrow lines. Xi sits about 2400 ppm above the moment-derived frequency because the reference complex is strongly deshielded.

Electron-capture nuclide, magnetic moment +4.720(10) nuclear magnetons. Used as a gamma-camera flood source and as the parent of the 14.4 keV Mossbauer line of 57Fe. Q not confidently tabulated, so null.
Integer spin I = 5. The radiotherapy workhorse (Gamma Knife, cobalt teletherapy) and a major industrial irradiation source. Q not confidently tabulated, so null.

name: Nickel
blurb: Nickel is a shielding and implant metal: it is the main ingredient of mu-metal magnetic shielding and of nitinol stents and guidewires, and it is ferromagnetic in bulk with a Curie temperature of 631 K. 61Ni is a difficult NMR nucleus, 1.14 percent abundant with a 16.2 fm2 quadrupole moment, and is confined to specialist solid-state work.
mrNotes: Mu-metal (about 77 percent Ni, 16 percent Fe) is the passive magnetic shielding wrapped around photomultipliers and electronics in PET/MR and around sensitive instruments near the fringe field.

Nitinol (NiTi) stents and guidewires are not ferromagnetic at all, only weakly paramagnetic at about +230 to +250 ppm SI, and are usually MR conditional, but they still cause local signal loss and can heat if they approach resonant length.
Bulk nickel is ferromagnetic, so nickel-plated tools, batteries and coins are projectile and torque hazards in Zone IV.
61Ni receptivity is about 0.24 times natural-abundance 13C, the lowest of any element in this row apart from 43Ca and 57Fe.

isotopes.notes: The only NMR-active stable Ni isotope. Solution spectra are limited to highly symmetric diamagnetic Ni(0) carbonyls and phosphines; the number of reported shifts is small enough that a representative range is not worth quoting, so shiftRange is null. Also the isotope used for synchrotron Mossbauer spectroscopy of nickel.

name: Copper
blurb: Copper is the conductor of MRI: RF transmit and receive coils, gradient windings and shields, RF screens and the shielded room are all copper. Its resistivity of 1.68e-8 ohm m sets coil Q, and its skin depth of about 8.2 um at 64 MHz and 5.8 um at 128 MHz sets the useful foil and trace thickness. 63Cu and 65Cu are both quadrupolar and observable only in high-symmetry Cu(I) sites.
mrNotes: Copper skin depth is about 8.2 um at 64 MHz (1.5 T) and 5.8 um at 128 MHz (3 T), so coil traces are typically 17 to 35 um foil, several skin depths thick.
Copper is diamagnetic, volume susceptibility about -9.6 ppm SI, close enough to tissue and water that copper coil structures near the imaging volume do not appreciably distort B0.
RF shielded rooms use continuous copper sheet or fine mesh; gradient shields are copper too, where eddy-current decay, not resistance, is the design constraint.
64Cu (t1/2 12.7 h, beta plus and beta minus) is a widely used PET nuclide for antibody and peptide imaging, with 67Cu as its therapeutic partner.

isotopes.notes: Receptivity about 380 times natural-abundance 13C, but the -22 fm2 quadrupole moment means only tetrahedral or cubic Cu(I) gives observable lines; Cu(II) is paramagnetic and NMR-silent.

Higher gamma and slightly smaller Q than 63Cu, so it often gives the narrower line despite less than half the abundance; comparing the two linewidths at one field separates quadrupolar from magnetic broadening.

Integer spin I = 1, magnetic moment -0.2166 nuclear magnetons. A major PET nuclide (64Cu-DOTATATE, 64Cu-labelled antibodies) whose 12.7 h half-life suits slow-clearing biologics. Q not confidently tabulated, so null.

name: Zinc
blurb: Zinc is the second most abundant trace metal in the body, but Zn2+ is d10, diamagnetic and MR-silent, so zinc imaging relies on gadolinium chelates whose relaxivity changes on Zn2+ binding rather than on detecting zinc itself. 67Zn is 4.1 percent abundant with gamma of 2.67 MHz/T, among the least receptive stable nuclei.
mrNotes: Zn2+ produces no relaxation enhancement of its own, so Zn-responsive Gd(III) smart agents, which switch r1 by roughly a factor of two on binding, are the standard approach in pancreas and prostate work.
67Zn receptivity is about 0.69 times natural-abundance 13C; solid-state 67Zn NMR of enzymes and ZnO generally needs enrichment and 18.8 T or above.
65Zn (t1/2 244 d, 1.12 MeV gamma) is a zinc-metabolism tracer, not an imaging agent.
Brass and zinc-coated hardware are non-ferromagnetic but still conductive, so they can support RF eddy currents and cause local B1 shading.

isotopes.notes: Q revised from the older 15.0 fm2 to +12.2(10) fm2 by collinear laser spectroscopy; the smaller value slightly relaxes the symmetry requirement but 67Zn remains a low-gamma, low-receptivity nucleus.
